candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Deuteronomy
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Deuteronomy, on 27:11-26. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13. PD. Cf. Gal 3:10 (verbatim Pauline citation).
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Deuteronomy (c. 365 AD)

On 'Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them' (Deu 27:26), Ephrem reads the final Ebal-curse as the canonical Old-Testament anchor of Paul's argument in Galatians 3:10 ('as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse: for it is written, Cursed is every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them' — verbatim citation). The total-law requirement makes salvation-by-works impossible: no one keeps all things. The verse becomes the typological seed of the apostolic gospel of grace. Tewahedo soteriology cites Deu 27:26 + Gal 3:10 as the canonical doubled-witness that the law diagnoses the curse the Cross removes.

On 'Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them' (Deu 27:26), Ephrem reads the final Ebal-curse as the canonical Old-Testament anchor of Paul's argument in Galatians 3:10 ('as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse: for it is written, Cursed is every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them' — verbatim citation). The total-law requirement makes salvation-by-works impossible: no one keeps all things. The verse becomes the typological seed of the apostolic gospel of grace. Tewahedo soteriology cites Deu 27:26 + Gal 3:10 as the canonical doubled-witness that the law diagnoses the curse the Cross removes.
